in_text_mentions: l syndrome, carpal tunnel syndrome, C7 or C8 radiculopathy (sometimes coexisting with UNE), brachial plexopathy, or Pancoast's tumor invading its medial cord, generalized polyneuropathy, and tendinopathy (36). The UNE is often misdiagnosed as a golfer's elbow due to an intimate relationship between UN and the common flexor tendon (CFT) origin. Notably, in a case of UN instability, the nerve can be directly overlying the CFT during elbow flexion (Figure 5). In more severe cases, weakness and the UN's innervated muscle wasting can be apparent (the first dorsal interosseous muscle in particular).

plate_findings.evidence: The ulnar nerve thickened at the proximal end of the cubital canal in the transverse section.
Compression of the ulnar nerve by anomalous anconeus epitrochlearis muscle in cross-section.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a patient ultrasound image showing the ulnar nerve thickened within the cubital canal, a characteristic finding of Cubital Tunnel Syndrome. B: Panel B is a patient ultrasound image demonstrating variable nerve diameter changes (thickened and thinner) at a entrapment site, consistent with Cubital Tunnel Syndrome. C: Panel C is a patient ultrasound image showing the compression of the ulnar nerve due to an anomalous muscle structure, a specific cause of Cubital Tunnel Syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Gao et al. Ultrasound-Assisted Precise In Situ Decompression for Cubital Tunnel Syndrome.. Orthopaedic surgery 2021. doi:10.1111/os.12922. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound measure results before the operation. (A) The ulnar nerve thickened at the proximal end of the cubital canal in the transverse section. (B) The ulnar nerve became thinner and thicker at Osborne's ligament in the longitudinal section. (C) Compression of the ulnar nerve by anomalous anconeus epitrochlearis muscle in cross‐section. (D) The ulnar nerve was compressed by a deep square cyst in the longitudinal section. UN, Ulnar Nerve; OL, Olecranon; ME, Medial Epicondyle of Humerus.
in_text_mentions: ration. The proximal ulnar nerve was thickened to varying degrees. The maximum cross‐sectional area was 0.11–0.26 cm2, with an average of 0.16 ± 0.05 cm2. Ultrasound could diagnose the presence of compression, as well as accurately locate and identify the reason for compression (Fig. 1A–D). The entrapment sites around the cubital tunnel included one case at the medial muscular septum, two cases at arcade of Struthers, four cases at anconeus epitrochlearis muscle, five cases beside the cyst of the proximal FCU, and 44 cases localized in a tiny region from Osborne's ligament to two heads of FCU.
